result:
Design registered at `runs/pending_experiment.json`. Summary of this round's decision:

**Diagnosis.** Experiment 2 (grid classification + soft-argmax) was not actually refuted — the DB records it as a 1e9 fail, but `metrics.json` shows its real numbers: 743 m median error on confident frames (3.6× better than the kept baseline's 2675 m), both deployment gates passed, and the 1e9 came purely from the frozen coverage gate — only 10.75% of eval frames cleared the 0.3 confidence threshold, below the 20% minimum. Crucially, it trained for only **33 seconds** (8 harness epochs) with the loss still falling steeply, sitting ~3.8 nats above the soft-label entropy floor. Since its confidence *is* posterior neighborhood mass, an undertrained (diffuse) posterior mathematically guarantees low coverage — the gate failure and the accuracy ceiling plausibly share one cause.

**Experiment 3.** Re-land experiment 2's head byte-for-byte (including its confidence readout, deliberately unchanged as the control) and give it a real training budget: an internal ×12 epoch multiplier in `train.py` (96 effective epochs — a pattern loop.sh's comments already document), cosine LR decay 1e-3 → 1e-5, and fresh random rotations re-extracted every epoch instead of the baseline's single frozen rotation per crop. That last part matters because I confirmed the eval split is genuinely unseen territory (eval blocks never touched by any training window) with random headings — long training on frozen rotations would just memorize pixels.

**Pre-registered prediction:** coverage 0.4–0.8 and worst-case median error in the 250–600 m range (vs. 2674.93 m best). Falsifiable failure mode built in: if coverage again lands under 0.2 despite converged training loss, the neighborhood-mass confidence definition is cleanly indicted and the next round should redesign the readout, not the training. Expected wall-time ~15–25 min on local MPS; ONNX identical to experiment 2's (~2.5 MiB, ~0.6 ms), well inside gates.

The harness will now handle implementation, training, scoring, and the keep/revert call.
